items.title: Learner Driver Costs UK 2026: Licence, Theory and Practical Test Fees
items.description: Provisional licence £34-£43, theory test £23, practical test £62 on weekdays and £75 evenings, weekends and bank holidays. Free learner driver checklist.

items.title: Theory Test Pass Mark UK: 43 out of 50 and 44 out of 75
items.description: To pass the UK car theory test you need 43 out of 50 on multiple choice and 44 out of 75 on hazard perception. You must pass both parts.

items.title: How Many Driving Faults Can You Have and Still Pass?
items.description: To pass the UK practical driving test you can have no serious or dangerous faults and no more than 15 driving faults.

items.title: What to Take to Your UK Practical Driving Test
items.description: Photocard licence (or passport and paper licence), a car that meets the rules and proof of name change if needed. Free checklist.

items.title: Wrong Documents at Your Driving Test: Cancelled With No Refund
items.description: If you don't take the right items to your practical driving test, it will be cancelled and you won't get your money back.

items.title: The 4 Parts of the UK Practical Driving Test
items.description: Eyesight check, show me tell me questions, general and independent driving, and one reversing manoeuvre. About 35 minutes.

items.title: Driving Test Eyesight Check: 20 Metres
items.description: At the start of your practical test you must read a number plate from 20 metres, or 20.5 metres for old-style plates.

items.title: Independent Driving on the UK Driving Test
items.description: You'll follow a sat nav, road signs or both for 20 to 35 minutes. Taking a wrong turn isn't a fault.

items.title: Driving Test Manoeuvres: Which One Will You Get?
items.description: The reversing manoeuvre on the practical test is one of: parallel park, bay park, or pull up on the right and reverse.

items.title: How Long Is the UK Practical Driving Test?
items.description: The car practical driving test lasts about 35 minutes and has four parts.

items.title: How to Budget for Learning to Drive in the UK
items.description: List the licence and test fees, lessons, private practice fuel, insurance and extras, then track spend against a budget.

items.title: Failed Your Driving Test? Rebooking Rules and Cost
items.description: If you don't pass you pay the full test fee again, and you can rebook a date at least 10 working days away.

items.title: Theory Test Revision Topics Checklist (UK)
items.description: Fourteen theory test topics from alertness to vehicle loading. Rate your confidence in each and track revision.

items.title: When Are You Ready for Your Driving Test?
items.description: GOV.UK says to take your driving test when you can do everything without instruction. Rate each skill 1 to 5 to check.

items.title: Driving Lesson Tracker Spreadsheet (UK)
items.description: Log each lesson with hours, price, skills practised and confidence, and see total spend and average cost per hour.

items.title: Parents: How to Track the Cost of Driving Lessons
items.description: A learner driver planner shows lesson hours, total cost, average price per hour and what's left of your budget.

items.title: Private Practice Log for Learner Drivers
items.description: Keep a log of practice with a parent or friend: date, hours, miles, fuel cost and what you worked on.

items.title: Is There a Minimum Number of Driving Lessons?
items.description: There is no minimum number of lessons before you can book your practical test, according to GOV.UK.

items.title: Theory Mock Test Score Tracker
items.description: Log mock test scores from any licensed practice app against the official pass marks of 43 out of 50 and 44 out of 75.

items.title: Learning to Drive in the UK? Start Here
items.description: Start with the free learner driver journey checklist, then track lessons, costs and theory revision in the planner.
